title: Health
subtitle: La salud
review: Written by Claude in Latin American (Mexican) Spanish. Check the Spanish, the English and the notes before recording audio. English support only.

categories.desc: Telling someone you are not well, or better again.
cards: Sentirse: to feel. Me siento bien, me siento mal, me siento mejor.
Me siento mal. Creo que me voy a casa.
I feel sick. I think I'm going home.
A woman says estoy enferma. Estar, not ser: it is how you are now.
No voy a trabajar hoy. Estoy enferma.
I'm not going to work today. I'm sick.
A woman says estoy mareada. Also what you say when the car or the boat makes you feel sick.
I'm dizzy. I need to sit down.
— ¿Cómo sigues? — Ya me siento mejor, gracias.
— How are you doing? — I feel better now, thanks.

categories.desc: Saying where it hurts, and the illnesses everyone gets.
cards: Me duele + one thing: la cabeza, la garganta, el estómago. Me duelen + more than one: me duelen los pies.
Point to the place. Useful when you don't know the word.
— Where does it hurt? — It hurts here.
In Mexico, la gripa is the everyday word for a cold. Elsewhere: un resfriado, la gripe.
I have a cold. Don't come near me.
With tener and no article. In Mexico you also hear tengo calentura.
Tengo fiebre y me duele todo el cuerpo.
I have a fever and my whole body aches.
La tos: a cough. Toser: to cough.
Tengo mucha tos en la noche.
I cough a lot at night.

categories.en: At the doctor and the pharmacy
categories.fr: Con el doctor y en la farmacia
categories.desc: What you say, and what the doctor or pharmacist asks.
cards: I need to see a doctor.
Ver a + a person. In Mexico el doctor, la doctora are more common than el médico.
Tengo fiebre desde hace tres días. Necesito ver a un doctor.
I've had a fever for three days. I need to see a doctor.
The doctor's first question, with usted. To a friend: ¿qué tienes?
— What's the matter? — My stomach hurts.
Answer with desde: desde ayer, desde el lunes. Or desde hace: desde hace dos días, for two days.
¿Tiene algo para el dolor de cabeza?
Do you have something for a headache?
At the pharmacy. Algo para + the problem: algo para la tos, algo para la gripa.
Do you have something for a cough?
Tómese esto dos veces al día.
Tomar: to take medicine. Una vez, dos veces, tres veces al día.
Tómese esto dos veces al día, después de comer.
Take this twice a day, after eating.
A woman says soy alérgica. The doctor asks: ¿es alérgico a algo?
— ¿Es alérgica a algo? — Sí, soy alérgica a la penicilina.
— Are you allergic to anything? — Yes, I'm allergic to penicillin.

categories.desc: Asking if someone is all right, wishing them well, and calling for help.
cards: You look pale. Are you all right?
Mejorarse: to get better. With usted: que se mejore.
Get plenty of rest. Get well soon!
With usted, to a stranger. In Mexico the emergency number is 911.
